_what: The ontology of the sentence-level build: every KIND of unit and relation that tools/placeholders.py produces, declared once, with the verse that forced it into existence. Doug, 2026-09-24: 'the ontology idea was mine and I think it is key to making this happen. I want you to build it out and make it visible to me as we discover structures working though verse by verse.'
_rules: BUILT FROM BELOW. A kind is admitted when a verse cannot be drawn without it, not written first and fitted to the text. Each entry names that verse.

CLOSED WORLD. tools/ontology.py reads the whole graph and fails on any node, edge or force value this file does not declare, and on any kind marked built that has no instances. The file cannot drift from the graph in either direction.

STATUS IS A FACT. built = the graph has instances now. proposed = on the queue in docs/BACKLOG.md, not built. superseded = built, still in the graph, due to be retired. withdrawn = tried and reversed; kept, with why, so nobody re-proposes it as the safe option. deferred = built before, by the earlier builder, and not by the clean one yet; its rule kept as code for re-entry (plan 1.27, the deferred registry), with `deferred` saying why, and whether the structure sweep supplies it meanwhile as a reading. Doug's word of 2026-10-15; applied as 'held' on 2026-10-17 and renamed the next day, since docs/HELD.md's held readings are another thing (plan 1.42).
REFS ARE MACULA'S. Hebrew verse numbers where they differ from English: Exo.8.6 here is the BSB's Exodus 8:10.
A READING IS NOT A KIND. 'Cause', 'motivation', 'execution' name what a reader infers over a structure. They enter as specializations only when the text marks them or a measured rule does.

KINDS ARE POLYMORPHIC (PRINCIPLES 47). A node's kind is the most specific the graph's current state supports, and is refined in place as layers arrive — an assertion becomes an illustration when the meaning graph sees the category clash. A pattern slot typed with a kind matches it or any specialization: tools/ontology.py `is_a` and `lineage`.

TYPES AND ROLES ARE KEPT APART. A kind says what a node IS, wherever it stands (a content that is an Action; an Author). A role says what it is IN A RELATION (the effect of `causes`; the basis or aim of a command; the voice of a Writing), and belongs on the relation. 'An action effect' is an Action in the effect role — never a kind of its own. The psalmist is a voice that RESOLVES TO David, not a subclass of David. The ontology discipline OntoClean's lesson, adopted 2026-09-25 (plan N.2) because it was free: ActionEffect had fused the two within a day of being proposed.

DOMAIN AND RANGE ARE CHECKED. Every relation's `from` and `to` — a kind or a list of kinds, matched by subsumption — is enforced on every edge. Adopted 2026-09-25 (plan N.1): declared and only drawn, they had let 7,653 second verb roles through.

layers.label: Meaning
layers.what: Language-independent: what a clause says, what force it is said with, and how clauses group. Patterns are matched here, so a Hebrew and a Greek passage can be the same shape.

layers.label: Language
layers.what: How Hebrew, Aramaic and Greek mark the upper layer: verb forms, connective words, word order. A Hebrew wayyiqtol and a Greek aorist indicative are different forms that may do the same thing.

layers.label: Words
layers.what: The word occurrences themselves, with lemma, Strong's number and morphology, as MACULA gives them. To become its own asset — the WORD GRAPH: every occurrence and lexeme with a stable source id, each attribute sourced, frozen and versioned, which the structure and meaning layers reference by id (docs/BACKLOG.md, 2026-09-25).

classes.label: Unit
classes.definition: Anything the graph holds a node for. Abstract: nothing is a bare Unit.

classes.label: Word occurrence
classes.definition: One word at one place in one verse. No identity across verses is claimed; 'the LORD' in Gen 2:4 and in Exo 8:6 are two nodes until a later pass merges them with evidence.

attrs.text: this occurrence's English rendering (MACULA `english`) — not the BSB's word, which the BSB verse contains only 60% of the time where the renderings differ
attrs.usual: the rendering MACULA's `english` gives this Hebrew word MOST OFTEN across the Hebrew Bible (the word card's 'most often rendered'), kept on common nouns and adjectives where it says more than this occurrence's: 'resting place' where Psa 23:2 has 'quiet' (Doug, 2026-09-26: 'going with the Hebrew is preferable'). Diagrams draw 'usually: resting place / here: quiet'. Not labelled 'from Hebrew': the usual rendering is not always the literal one (פָּנִים, 'face', is most often 'presence'). 28,888.

classes.label: Coordinated words
classes.definition: Words joined by 'and' and taken as one participant: 'the heavens and the earth', 'Moses and Aaron'. The only noun-phrase grouping built so far; each member hangs off it by `member`. Also MINTED where the text refers to a group it never names together: the doers of a fulfilled command ('they did so', Exo 8:13 → Moses and Aaron, the addressees down the command chain), marked `minted_for`.

established.note: flat layer, before the clause layer existed

classes.label: Referents taken together
classes.definition: A minted composite made by the structure sweep: one pronoun or unstated subject that stands for several the text names apart, each hanging off it by `member`. Matthew 20:18's 'we' is Jesus and the twelve of 20:17. Always a reading.

established.note: Declared by plan 1.43 (the closed world over the readings); made since the sweep's import of 2026-10-17.

classes.label: Described, not named
classes.definition: Someone the text describes but does not name, named by the sweep in its own words ('his armor-bearer', 'one of the priests carried off from Samaria'), so that the pronouns that stand for them have a referent. Linked to the text's own word where it names the same person or group (`refers_to`), or the group they are one of (`partitive`). Always a reading.

established.note: Declared by plan 1.43; made by the sweep's resolution pass since 2026-10-17, checked against the text's own words by plan 1.41.

classes.label: Clause
classes.definition: One act of saying something: a content, said with a force. The unit the rest of the structure groups.

established.why: 'said' had nowhere to point. The verb was an edge label, so 'God said' could not take 'let there be light' as what was said.

classes.falsified_by: A verse whose meaning needs a unit smaller than MACULA's clause and larger than a phrase.

classes.label: Content
classes.definition: What a clause says, without the force: a predicate and its participants. Two clauses that say the same thing with different force share a content KEY.

established.quote: "thanks to the Lord" is the lowest level grouping

classes.proof: Gen 1:3: 'let there be light' and 'there was light' have one key, s=light v=הָיָה, and differ only in force (jussive, wayyiqtol). 38% of content keys recur.
classes.falsified_by: Two clauses with the same key that a reader would say do not say the same thing.

classes.label: Verb
classes.definition: The predicate of a clause as a node, carrying its form (mood, stem, person) so it can be pointed at.
classes.was: A kind beside Word (parent Unit), when the earlier builder made a verb node of its own. In the clean builder the verb is a word node with its form on it, so a Verb is a Word; beside it, every verb was counted as a plain word and 93,080 predicates looked out of place (plan 1.42, 2026-10-17).

established.quote: let's start with just "give thanks to the lord"

classes.label: Ordered pair
classes.definition: Two units taken together, in an order that matters, with one of them the head. A group keeps its head's force. Abstract: every group is one of the specializations below.

established.quote: order does matter with this pattern so it is more than just a pair

classes.also: Doug, 2026-09-21: 'imparative modified as a basis is still an imperative by the way' — the group keeps its head's force.

classes.label: Action, then state
classes.deferred: Built by the earlier builder (tools/placeholders.py); the clean builder (plan 1.26) does not build it yet. Its rule, measurements and tests are kept as code for re-entry (plan 1.27). Meanwhile the structure sweep supplies it as a reading, shown as automated analysis (plan 1.34, out/sweep-layer.jsonl.gz).
classes.definition: A command, then the same act reported as having happened. The order is the content: reversed, it would be an act followed by a command to do it.

established.quote: simplified to action and then state grouped together - a particular type of pair

classes.rule: A jussive / imperative / cohortative, then a later wayyiqtol of the same lemma, within 4 verses — done by the one commanded (or, for a causative, by what the command acts on), and for a command to speak TO someone, spoken to that same someone. Where an actor is unknown the pair stands.
classes.was: Same lemma alone, until 2026-09-24: in the frog plague 3 of 5 cross-verse pairs were false (the magicians' 'brought up'; 'say to Aaron' paired with Pharaoh's and Moses's 'he said').
classes.falsified_by: A pair whose second member is not done by the one commanded.

classes.label: Imperative, and what qualifies it
classes.definition: A command as a unit: the first members are the command — ONE command, or a COLLECTION of commands joined by 'and' at one speech level ('stretch out your staff AND strike the dust', Exo 8:12; Doug: 'the second level (aaron) imperative content is a collection of 2 actions') — and every further member is a QUALIFIER the text attaches to them, typed by what it does. A saying's `content` points at the group, not at its first command. A group may have no qualifier: a collection alone is one. One class, extended by qualifier types rather than specialized into a class per combination — a command often carries several at once. The group keeps the command's force: qualified, it is still a command.

established.quote: it seems that there should be one imperative class with either specializations or extendibility

extension_points: basis — a stated reason, כִּי (built; Psa 107:1)
aim — a purpose: a command, then waw + jussive / cohortative / yiqtol in another person (built; Exo 7:26 'that they may serve me')
effect — what the commanded act brings about: a command, then waw + a third-person weqatal (built 2026-09-25; Exo 8:12 'strike the dust ... and it will become gnats'; 10 of 14)
warning — the consequence of refusing it: a condition that refuses the command's own verb (proposed; Exo 7:27)
promise — the consequence of obeying it, 'if you obey ... then' (not yet proposed: the draft rule cannot separate it from noise)
classes.also: Doug, 2026-09-21: 'imparative modified as a basis is still an imperative by the way' — the principle the whole class rests on.
classes.falsified_by: A qualifier that changes what the command IS rather than adding to it — which would make it a different kind, not an extension.

classes.label: Imperative, and its basis
classes.definition: A command and the reason the text gives for it, as its own class.

established.quote: the qualified imperative has a reason and they are grouped together by something similar to the action/state pair ... but it is not quite action/state - it is imperative/basis

classes.instead: Imperative, with `basis` as one of its qualifier types (2026-09-25). As a class of its own it would have needed a sibling for every other qualifier, and a class for every combination of them.

classes.label: Condition, then consequence
classes.definition: An 'if' clause and the clause it conditions, as one node: 1 = the condition, 2 = the consequence. The group keeps the consequence's force — it is the clause that asserts or commands; the condition only says when.

established.quote: the entry point is the if/then and the "let them go" is part of the refusal clause under the if condition

classes.was: Only an `if` edge between the two clauses, so a speech turn could point at nothing but its loose clauses — 7:27 showed as two unrelated parts of the Lord's speech.

classes.label: Imperative, and the consequence of refusing it
classes.instead: The `warning` qualifier of Imperative (2026-09-25): the same rule, as a member type rather than a class. Everything below is kept as the record of how it was found.
classes.definition: A command, then a condition whose protasis is that same command REFUSED — the command's own verb under 'refuse' (מָאֵן) or 'not' — and whose apodosis is what will follow. The group keeps the imperative's force: a warning attached to a command is still a command, as a basis is.

established.quote: looking at BSB 8:2 it is a continuation of the Lord's speech, but also a motivation/consequence of not following the imperative

classes.evidence: STATED, not inferred: 'if you refuse TO LET THEM GO' repeats 'LET my people GO' (שָׁלַח) from 7:26 and negates it. That shared verb is what separates this from a reading. 'Motivation' is what a reader calls the effect of the pair — the reading layer; 'warning' is what the text states.
classes.proof: 16 in the Hebrew Bible by the draft rule — a floor, since a condition introduced by כִּי אִם (Exo 9:2) is taken as a different connective. The same shape three times in the plague cycle: frogs (Exo 7:26-27), flies (8:16-17), locusts (10:3-4); also Gen 20:7 'return the man's wife ... if you do not return her, you will surely die'.
classes.mirror: The compliance side — 'if you obey ... then' — is the same structure with the protasis affirmative, and is where covenant blessing lives (Exo 19:5, Deu 28). The draft rule finds 47 candidates there but most are noise (Gen 15:5 'count the stars — if you are able to count them'), so it is not proposed until it can be separated.
classes.falsified_by: A command followed by a negated condition on its own verb whose consequence is NOT tied to the refusal — a condition that merely reuses the verb.
classes.rule: A held `if` edge whose protasis (with its infinitive complement) contains the lemma of a command within the previous 40 clauses of the same book, the protasis being refusal (מָאֵן) or negated. Group: 1 = the command, 2 = the consequence (the `if` source), with the condition reachable through the `if` edge.

classes.deferred: Built by the earlier builder (tools/placeholders.py); the clean builder (plan 1.26) does not build it yet. Its rule, measurements and tests are kept as code for re-entry (plan 1.27). Meanwhile the structure sweep supplies it as a reading, shown as automated analysis (plan 1.34, out/sweep-layer.jsonl.gz).
classes.definition: Two lines where the second states the first's roles minus the subject, because it is the same subject. The subject sits on the group AND is carried to each line: both readings are true.

established.quote: word is the subject for the collection

classes.also: Doug: 'lamp for feet and light for path do each stand on their own', and 'the verse could read "your word is a light and lamp" and it would still be valid' — the test that the collection is right.
classes.falsified_by: A second line with no subject of its own whose subject is NOT the first line's.

classes.deferred: Built by the earlier builder (tools/placeholders.py); the clean builder (plan 1.26) does not build it yet. Its rule, measurements and tests are kept as code for re-entry (plan 1.27). Meanwhile the structure sweep supplies it as a reading, shown as automated analysis (plan 1.34, out/sweep-layer.jsonl.gz).
classes.definition: Consecutive 'the one who ...' clauses (participles used as nouns, each folded out of its '[he is] ...' frame) describing one referent, across verses within a chapter: Psa 103:3-5 'who forgives all your iniquity, who heals all your diseases, who redeems your life from the pit, who crowns you ..., who satisfies you with good'. The group's subject is the common referent (the first description's unstated 'he'); each description keeps its own subject node.

established.quote: psalm 103: 3- needs to have a subject node for each of the parts in vs 3-5 or it needs to have a collection and a common subject that applies to all - either way the subject node is missing and that was never the intent

classes.label: Concession: the obstacle, what holds anyway, and why
classes.deferred: Built by the earlier builder (tools/placeholders.py); the clean builder (plan 1.26) does not build it yet. Its rule, measurements and tests are kept as code for re-entry (plan 1.27). Meanwhile the structure sweep supplies it as a reading, shown as automated analysis (plan 1.34, out/sweep-layer.jsonl.gz).
classes.definition: Where the text marks a concession (גַּם כִּי, 'even though'): the conceded clause (the obstacle), the claim that holds anyway, and — where a כִּי gives it — that claim's ground. Where the held claim is NEGATED, the response the obstacle would have brought is named by the text and denied, and the group carries it as `denied`: Psa 23:4 'even though I walk through the valley of deep darkness, I will NOT FEAR harm, for you are with me' → conceded, holds anyway, its ground; denied 'fear'. That this is an overridden motivation is the reading over the group (meaning graph). The mirror of `failed_result`: there an act's aim does not come; here a circumstance's expected outcome does not, and the text says why.

established.quote: "Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death" is in effect an obstacle overcome - an overridden motivation

classes.also: Built only on גַּם כִּי. A fronted כִּי is when / if / though undecided, and a negated main clause does not decide it ('if you meet anyone, do not greet him', 2Ki 4:29). גַּם alone is 'also' far more often than 'even if'.
classes.proof: 6 built; 5 concessions (Psa 23:4, Pro 22:6, Isa 1:15, Hos 8:10, 9:16) and 1 wrong: Rut 2:21 'he ALSO told me' — גַּם כִּי there is 'also' + the saying. Denied response named in 3 (fear, depart, listen); a ground in 1 (Psa 23:4).

classes.label: Acts of one agent
classes.deferred: Built by the earlier builder (tools/placeholders.py); the clean builder (plan 1.26) does not build it yet. Its rule, measurements and tests are kept as code for re-entry (plan 1.27). Meanwhile the structure sweep supplies it as a reading, shown as automated analysis (plan 1.34, out/sweep-layer.jsonl.gz).
classes.definition: Clauses in a row that are the acts of one agent: joined by no word, none a narrative 'and then' (wayyiqtol), each stating its subject only in its verb, and every one of those subjects resolved to the SAME referent. The agent sits on the group (`group_subject`), as a Parallel's subject does; the acts are its members (`agent_act`), in order. A run crosses verses within a chapter. Psalm 23:2-3: 'he makes me lie down / he leads me / he restores my soul / he guides me' — four acts of the LORD.

established.quote: verses 2-3 could be a collection of 4 actions of the Lord with a single subject. Structurally they fit a similar pattern surround by first person I statements

classes.also: Doug chose a new group over widening Parallel ('agree - build it as a new group, acts of one agent'): Parallel's lines repeat the same roles, and these do not — lie down in pastures, lead beside waters, restore a soul, guide in paths. The first-person statements around the run are the proposed Context kind, which he set after the meaning graph.
classes.proof: Measured before building: 207 runs keyed on the referent's lemma (134 of 2, 42 of 3, 17 of 4, up to 11), 189 in the Psalms, where the addressee and pronoun rules reach. A glance at 10 found 3 wrong, all from the pronoun resolution beneath it (Psa 4:5's 'you' is the people, not God; 125:1's 'it' is Zion): the group's precision is the pronoun rules'.
classes.falsified_by: A run whose acts are one agent's but that the text divides — a clause between them, or a narrative sequence — or a run joined only because two different referents share a node.

classes.label: Episode
classes.definition: A run of clauses one rung above the sentence. Hypothesis: וַיְהִי + a time phrase opens one (27.9% open a Berean section against 11.5% for other wayyiqtol). A signal, not a rule.

established.note: journal, 'what marks an episode?'

classes.label: Communication unit
classes.definition: Someone communicating something to someone: a SENDER, an ADDRESSEE, what is communicated (its parts), a MEDIUM (speech or writing) and a MODE (performed — it happens in the text; commanded — a directive to communicate, which may be fulfilled later or not at all). Communications NEST: every one except the outermost is a part of an enclosing communication, and the chain rolls all the way up to the writer of the scroll, the psalm or the letter. Abstract: every communication is one of the specializations below.

established.quote: make sure that the ontology fully supports the concept of nested speech where speech is really a form of communication that rolls all the way up to the writer of the scroll

classes.also: Doug, the same day: 'speech is a communication unit - writing a scroll/psalm/letter to a church is a communication unit.' And on the frog plague: 'the real speech turn is God to Moses - the Moses speech turn is actually a directive from God which Moses does not fulfill in these verses - though it is a speech turn, regardless.'
classes.example: Exodus 7:26-29 (BSB 8:1-4): [the writer of Exodus -> its readers: [the LORD -> Moses, performed: [Moses -> Pharaoh, commanded: [thus says the LORD: let my people go ... if you refuse ... the frogs will come up on you]]]].
extension_points: medium — speech (built, as Speech turn) or writing (the Writing unit, proposed); a written communication can also be nested, as a letter quoted in a narrative (Ezra 4) or 'write this in a book' (Exo 17:14)
mode — performed or commanded (built); a commanded communication's fulfilment is a later performed one, which is not yet linked
sender, addressee — edges to who the text names (built where stated or inferred by a written rule); left empty rather than guessed
reported — speech described but not quoted ('he told them all these words'); not yet a kind
classes.falsified_by: A quoted speech that belongs to no sender at any level up to the writing — which would mean a communication with no source.

classes.label: Writing (scroll, psalm, letter)
classes.built_for: The Psalms first (2026-09-25): one Writing per psalm, minted at its first verse; `frame` to each heading clause; `sender` to the person the heading names; `part` to every top-level unit of every verse. Doug, on Psalm 23: 'the assertion that this is a psalm of David needs to inform all nodes in the scroll.' The heading also informs the psalm's own voice: a first-person singular clause outside any quoted speech, with no subject of its own, takes the writer as its inferred subject. Other books wait for re-keying by span.
classes.definition: The outermost communication: the book, psalm or letter as a unit, from its writer to its readers. Every speech with no enclosing speech is a part of it, and narration is its own voice. The SENDER is set only where the text states one — 'Paul, an apostle ... to the church of God in Corinth' (1 Cor 1:1-2), a psalm's heading — and left open where it does not: the text of Exodus names no writer, so the graph names none.

established.quote: the assertion that this is a psalm of David needs to inform all nodes in the scroll

classes.rule: One per book; per psalm in Psalms. A top-level speech turn is `part` of it.
classes.caution: The heading's לְדָוִד can be read 'of', 'for' or 'about' David. The sender edge carries the preposition and says it is taken as authorship, which is Doug's reading and the traditional one.
classes.addressee: Doug, 2026-09-25: 'each scroll has an author and potentially an addressee ... e.g. church of Corinth when we get to the NT.' A Writing's addressee is set only where the text states one — 'to the church of God in Corinth' (1 Cor 1:2), 'to Theophilus' (Luke 1:3) — as its author is. Not built: the Psalms state none, and the letters are step 3 (Greek).
classes.why_not_built_elsewhere: A book-level node breaks the assumption, everywhere downstream, that a node's ref is a verse — which is exactly what PRINCIPLES 46 says to remove. The psalm is small enough to be minted in its first verse, as the speech turn is; the books wait for re-keying by span (docs/BACKLOG.md).

classes.label: Author (the voice of a writing)
classes.definition: The authoring voice of a Writing — the role, as distinct from the person who fills it. The writing's own 'I' and 'my' point here; the voice resolves to a named person only at the highest level, the Writing, where the text itself names one (`resolves_to`): a psalm's heading, a letter's greeting ('Paul, an apostle'). Never by tradition. Abstract: each author voice is one of the specializations below; built for psalms so far.

established.quote: is psalmist generic enough for the whole graph or is it a special case that we can justify establishing? ... I think it is a specialization of scroll author

extension_points: psalmist — the voice of a psalm (built)
narrator — the voice of a narrative book, which names no writer (not yet)
letter writer — 'Paul, an apostle ... to the church of God in Corinth' (not yet; Greek)
the Teacher — Qoheleth, who names himself in Ecclesiastes 1:1 (not yet)

classes.label: Psalmist
classes.definition: The Author of a psalm. One per psalm, headed or not. The psalm's 'I' and 'my', outside any quoted speech, point to the psalmist; the psalmist resolves to the heading's name at the Writing level.

established.quote: this is a psalm that each of us can read so "David" needs to be held lightly - whoever is praying this psalm can substitute themselves - I would rather say the psalmist and let it resolve in the highest level context to David

classes.why: A psalm is written to be prayed. Resolving its 'I' straight to David made every reader's prayer a statement about David; resolving it to the voice keeps the text's own claim ('the LORD is my shepherd') for whoever speaks it, while the heading still says whose voice it first was.
classes.matched_by: The clean builder's voice node (Psa.10.1#psalmist: `voice`, local name `psalmist`); the earlier builder's `author_kind` it was matched by is gone, and the 66 voices and the 842 'I's resolved to them looked undeclared (plan 1.42, 2026-10-17).

classes.label: Address (a turn to 'you')
classes.deferred: Built by the earlier builder (tools/placeholders.py); the clean builder (plan 1.26) does not build it yet. Its rule, measurements and tests are kept as code for re-entry (plan 1.27).
classes.definition: A run of clauses marked second person — verbs, pronouns, suffixes — outside any quoted speech, inside a Writing: the writer turning to address someone. Nested in the Writing as one of its parts; sender the writer. Built for the Psalms.

established.quote: but then there is a flip to directly addressing God as "you"

classes.open: The ADDRESSEE is left empty: 'you' has no antecedent in the text, only an addressee, and who it is (the LORD, in Psalm 23) is a matter for the meaning graph. Parked with the context-setting bundle (docs/BACKLOG.md).

classes.label: Assertion
classes.definition: A clause said with assertive force — it states that something is, was or will be so — as against a directive ('let my people go') or a wish. Derived from the clause's form through the language layer (see `forces`): a wayyiqtol, qatal, yiqtol, weqatal, a predicating participle, a Greek indicative, or a verbless clause asserts. The parent of Illustration.

established.quote: the ontology still labels assertion as proposed - aren't we beyond that?

classes.proof: 90,182 of 114,573 clauses (Hebrew 71,347, Greek 18,835) — against 9,350 directives and 15,041 non-finite or wishes. Doug: 'assertions will dominate'.
classes.asserter: Every assertion is made by SOMEONE: the sender of the innermost communication it sits in — the speaker, inside a speech turn; the author (narrator) outside one. Doug, 2026-09-25: 'all narratives are assertions by the scroll author or speaker.' Built for the Psalms (the psalmist); for narrative books it waits on the narrator voice (Author, extension point) and the book-level Writing.

classes.label: Directive
classes.definition: A clause said with directive force — it tells someone to do or be something: an imperative, a jussive ('let there be light'), a cohortative ('let us'), a Greek imperative or hortatory subjunctive. The head of an Imperative group is one.

established.note: 'let there be light' — the jussive that separated command from report on the first day the clause layer was built.

classes.label: Question
classes.definition: A clause said with interrogative force: it asks. Marked in the Hebrew by an interrogative word (מִי 'who', מָה 'what / why', אֵיךְ 'how', אַיֵּה 'where', לָמָּה / מַדּוּעַ 'why') or the prefixed interrogative הֲ. Derived from form in the clean builder's stage S2 (docs/BUILDER-DESIGN.md). Before it, the graph had no question force at all: every one of 2,213 interrogatives stood in a clause marked assertion (invariants baseline, 2026-09-27).

established.quote: question force: add it

classes.label: Illustration (a symbolic assertion)
classes.definition: An assertion made through an image rather than concretely: 'the LORD is my shepherd'. A specialization of assertion — the claim is true, but by likeness: the LORD is not a shepherd, and says more by being called one. Doug: 'more powerful than trying to be concrete and makes up most of the psalms.'

established.quote: I ready think that we can categorize "the Lord is my Shepherd" as a specialization of assertion which is symbolic or analogous in nature - it is not a concrete assertion - it is really an "illustration"

classes.structural_base: The X-is-Y construction with a nominal predicate — out/metaphor.jsonl.gz, 3,536 clauses, tenor and vehicle — which HOLDS Psalm 23:1 ('LORD = my shepherd'). But that layer says of itself that it 'does NOT claim every row is figurative: the man is a prophet predicates a real category and nothing structural separates it'. A sample of 16 of its rows: about 6 figurative ('you are our potter', 'the crown of the wise is their wealth'), the rest literal ('they are my people', 'two and a half cubits long').
classes.why_not_built: What separates an illustration from a concrete predication is a CATEGORY CLASH — the LORD is not in the category 'shepherd' — which is the meaning graph's to see. Doug's reading of Psalm 23:1 is recorded as held reading doug-043 and is the first case to test it on; it is not a rule. His hypothesis that illustration 'makes up most of the psalms' becomes measurable once it is.
extension_points: metaphor ('you are our potter') — the X-is-Y case, at the level of a CLAUSE
simile ('like an earring of gold is a wise man's rebuke') — marked by 'like'/'as', and so partly structural
the extended picture — the shepherd of Psalm 23:1-4 carried through pastures, waters, paths, rod and staff — which is the Context kind's scope

the PARABLE — an illustration at the level of a whole COMMUNICATION: a told story that stands for something (Nathan's ewe lamb, 2 Sam 12; the vineyard, Isa 5; the parables of the Gospels). Doug, 2026-09-25: 'parables are illustrations'. The same kind at two levels — the polymorphism of PRINCIPLES 47 — so a pattern over illustrations can meet a metaphor and a parable alike.

classes.label: Action (a content that is a doing)
classes.definition: A content whose predicate is something done: 'me lie down in green pastures' (Psa 23:2), 'the frogs go up' (Exo 8:2). A TYPE — what the content is, wherever it stands. 'An action effect', Doug's words for 23:2, is an Action in the effect role of `causes`: the type and the role are asked for separately, so a pattern can want either (PRINCIPLES 47).

established.quote: in this case it is an action effect

classes.why_not_built: Action or state is a fact about the VERB, not the clause, and nothing on the Hebrew side marks it: MACULA gives an agent frame (A0) to 'be holy' (11/11) and 'be strong' (81/82) exactly as to 'lie down' (24/24), and the stative vowel patterns miss statives like gadal. Of 3,240 causatives across 155 roots, most are motion (bring in 476, bring back 309, bring out 250, bring up 222) but states are mixed in (multiply 84, make king 45, provoke 41, strengthen 33, make good 30). The word graph (step 2) holds the fact per lemma; classifying verb types is a substep of step 5 (plan 5.5). Held readings: doug-049 (23:2, an action effect), doug-050 (23:3, a state — life replenished).

classes.label: State (a content that is a condition)
classes.definition: A content whose predicate is a condition rather than a doing: 'multiply', 'be strong', 'be angry', 'be king' — and, in Doug's reading of Psalm 23:3, a depleted life replenished. A TYPE; in the effect role of `causes` it is what was called a state effect. Sibling of Action.
classes.why_not_built: See Action: the line is lexical, and it is taken up in step 5.

classes.label: Action effect
classes.definition: Proposed 2026-09-25 as a kind of Content: the effect of a causative that is itself an action ('he makes me LIE DOWN', Psa 23:2).
classes.withdrawn: The same day, in the review against ontology practice (plan N.2): it FUSED a type with a role. Whether a content is an action is what it is; being an effect is its place in a `causes` relation. Fused, a pattern could not ask for 'any action' or 'any effect' without enumerating the crossings, and every new role (basis, aim, condition) would multiply the kinds. Replaced by the type Action, in the effect role of `causes`. Do not re-propose a Role+Type kind: declare the type, and let the relation carry the role.

classes.label: State effect
classes.definition: Proposed 2026-09-25 beside ActionEffect: the effect of a causative that is a condition.
classes.withdrawn: Fused type and role, as ActionEffect. Replaced by the type State, in the effect role of `causes`.

classes.label: Context-setting clause and its scope
classes.definition: A clause that sets the context in which following clauses are read — 'the LORD is my shepherd' for Psalm 23:1-4 — and the span it governs. 'I shall not want' is read in its light (because the LORD is my shepherd, I lack nothing), though nothing connects them in the Hebrew.

established.quote: verse 1 then presents the first challenge of context setting - I shall not want needs to be read in the context of "the Lord is my shepherd"

classes.also: Doug's anecdote: reading the KJV as a child he took it as 'the Lord is my shepherd, [whom] I shall not want' — the second clause as the object of the first. The Hebrew keeps them as sibling clauses, and so does the graph; what it cannot yet say is how the first governs the second.
classes.why_not_built: Its SCOPE is found by meaning, not grammar: the shepherd picture runs through v4 (pastures, waters, paths, rod and staff) and a host picture takes over in v5 (table, oil, cup) — whether 'shepherd' governs vv5-6 Doug leaves open. The pronoun chain shows who acts throughout, not which picture governs. Doug: 'mark this as something to come back to after the meaning graph is done and we are putting it all together - we can only go so far based on the base structure ontology rules.'

classes.label: Speech turn
classes.definition: A communication by speech, however many verses it runs. Open at the end of a verse that holds a speech and does not end on a narrative wayyiqtol outside it; continued by each following verse that does not open with a narrative wayyiqtol. TURNS NEST: the outermost is opened by a narrated saying that sits inside no speech; each saying inside its speech opens the next turn in, which is a `part` of the one around it. Each turn has a mode (performed / commanded) and, where the text gives them, a sender and an addressee. Continuing verses are parts of the innermost turn.
classes.nesting: Built 2026-09-25 after Doug: 'the real speech turn is God to Moses - the Moses speech turn is actually a directive from God'. The first version kept ONE turn per verse, opened at the last saying ('thus says the LORD'), so the LORD-to-Moses turn did not exist. A first nesting build looped forever — a saying reachable from its own speech — and ran past 400s; frames already on the stack are never re-entered.

established.note: The frog plague overview held YHWH's message to Pharaoh (7:26-7:29) as five unconnected groups, because every clause link stops at a verse boundary and a speech does not. Doug: 'build the speech turn across verses next'.

classes.rule: frame = the LAST saying in the opening verse (the innermost, so a message inside a message belongs to its own speaker); part = every clause of a continuing verse that nothing else in that verse points at.
classes.falsified_by: A verse opening with a non-wayyiqtol clause that is narrative background, not speech — 'Now Moses was eighty years old' after a speech — which the rule would wrongly take as the speech continuing.
classes.proof: Random sample of 14 turns against the Berean text: 12 right. First build 9 of 12, and its longest turns ran 150-188 verses through Proverbs and across psalms — any speech verb with a content edge could open one. Now only a narrated saying (wayyiqtol or qatal) opens a turn, a continuing verse stops at its first narrative wayyiqtol, and each psalm starts fresh.
classes.known_fault: The falsifier happens. Hebrew has no mark for where a quotation ends, so a verse that opens with background after a speech is taken as the speech: 'Now Laban had two daughters' (Gen 29:16), and the psalmist's own voice after quoting the wicked (Psa 73:12) — 2 of the 14 sampled. And a narrated saying INSIDE a long discourse ('the LORD said to me' within Moses's address) opens a new turn that then claims the rest of it: the longest are Deuteronomy 18:18 (170 verses), Proverbs 26:14 (122), Ecclesiastes 6:4 (116).

classes.label: Head and qualifier
classes.definition: A noun phrase as its head plus what qualifies it: 'the houses OF your officials'. MACULA marks it NPofNP 54,333 times; we flatten it to one node.

established.quote: I think that psalm 107:1 is correct but the primitive nodes could be broken down further

classes.label: List
classes.definition: Items the text sets out one after another as a list, in order, with the clause that introduces them where there is one: a genealogy, the peoples of Acts 2:9-11, the names of the Twelve. A list's members are its `heading` (optional) and its `item`s. The heading, where there is one, is the group's head; a list without one is still a list. What each item is (a people group, a person) is said by the meaning layer (plan 1.41), not by the list.

established.note: Plan 1.35, first round: 769 of the sweep's none_fit notes were lists with nowhere to go. Doug took a group kind over entities only and over leaving lists ungrouped.

classes.label: Cause and effect
classes.definition: The first name for Gen 1:3's pair. Withdrawn because the text does not say the light came BECAUSE of the command; that is a reading.

established.quote: the call that and implies cause effect was inferred by me - might start as a simple pair until we get good at inferring such relationship.

classes.instead: ActionState. Cause is a further specialization that would attach to it, when something in the text marks it.

classes.label: State nested in its command
classes.definition: 'There was light' drawn as a child of 'let there be light'.

established.quote: "there was light" is the effect of God saying the command and not the command itself

relations.label: asserts
relations.definition: A clause says a content, with a force. The force is on this edge, not on the content, so one content can be commanded in one clause and reported in the next.
relations.was: Called `content` at first, which collided with the speech `content` edge.

relations.label: participant
relations.definition: The roles MACULA assigns inside a clause. The content is the hub; each role is an edge from it.

relations.label: verb
relations.widened: Plan 1.42, 2026-10-17: a predicate may be a list of verbs, as MACULA's VPandVP gives it ('right-handed and left-handed', 1 Chronicles 12:2), 413 in the clean builder. 2026-10-18: or a word MACULA itself puts in the verb role that is not a verb, 114: a verbal adjective ('Obadiah feared the LORD', יָרֵא, 1 Kings 18:3; 'clothed', לָבוּשׁ), a 'behold' (הִנֵּה, 26: see the `presented` mark), a few nouns. The original's role is kept; such a clause has no verb form (S2).
relations.known_fault: A handful are MACULA's tagging, not a predicate: καί (1 Corinthians 4:11) and οὐ in the verb role. Kept as the source gives them, noted here.

relations.label: subject
inferred_by: carried from the parallel line above
same actor as the command it is joined to
the psalmist — the psalm's own voice
nearest agreeing referent up the ordered chain
relations.note: An inferred subject is marked on the edge with the rule that inferred it. Doug, 2026-09-21: 'don't attribute until the context exists to do so'. An IMPLICIT subject is different — not inferred but stated: a finite verb with no subject word carries its subject's person, gender and number, and gets a pronoun node ('he', 'they', 'I') marked `implicit` (Psa 23:2 'HE makes me lie down'; Doug, 2026-09-25). Who that pronoun refers to is `refers_to`, proposed.

relations.label: predicate
relations.definition: The predicate of a verbless clause: 'your word is A LAMP'.

relations.label: prepositional
relations.definition: A participant through a preposition, which is kept: 'TO the LORD' and 'BEFORE the LORD' are different relations.

relations.label: object
relations.deferred: Built by the earlier builder (tools/placeholders.py); the clean builder (plan 1.26) does not build it yet. Its rule, measurements and tests are kept as code for re-entry (plan 1.27).
relations.definition: In a VERBLESS clause whose predicate is a prepositional phrase, the preposition does the verb's work and is the predicate node; this links it to its object. 'you [are] WITH me' (Psa 23:4): you ← is (no verb) → with (עִמָּד) → me. With a verb, the preposition stays on its role's edge ('leads me BESIDE waters'): there the verb is the claim.

established.quote: the Hebrew "עִמָּד with me with me" should be represented I think in the graph

relations.proof: 4,618 verbless clauses with a prepositional predicate ('[is] in', '[belongs] to', '[are] with'); before, the preposition was only a label on the predicate edge, glued to MACULA's supplied verb ('are.with').

relations.label: for the sake of
relations.deferred: Built by the earlier builder (tools/placeholders.py); the clean builder (plan 1.26) does not build it yet. Its rule, measurements and tests are kept as code for re-entry (plan 1.27).
relations.reads: {src} is done for the sake of {dst}
relations.definition: What an act is done FOR: its motive, marked by the text with לְמַעַן before a noun — 'he guides me in paths of righteousness FOR THE SAKE OF his name' (Psa 23:3), 'for the sake of the fifty' (Gen 18:24). A reading ('motivation') enters as a kind only where the text marks it; לְמַעַן is that mark. Before a CLAUSE the same word is 'so that', a purpose, and is not this.

established.quote: the "for sake of" ləmaʿan link seems to be missing - it is the motivation that links the action to the Lord's name

relations.label: refers to
relations.definition: Who (or what) a pronoun or pro-form is: 'he' (Psa 23:2) is the LORD (23:1). Four rules, all from Doug: (1) a SINGULAR third-person pronoun resolves only if EXACTLY ONE referent in the leading text — the last 12 clauses, same speech level — agrees with it in gender and number; with two or more it is held, not guessed. Predicates, headings, pronouns and the psalm's voice are not referents; a divine name is singular AND masculine, since its verbs are (left without a gender it agreed with 'she': Pro 9:2 'she has prepared her meat', Wisdom, → the LORD; 49 feminine pronouns → a divine name before, 14 after, all rule 2's; 2026-09-26); a resolved pronoun's referent stays in the leading text. A PLURAL 'they' is held (see known_fault). (2) In a psalm's own voice, an implicit 'you' inside an address is that address's addressee: God by default, or a vocative beside the clause ('Bless the LORD, O my soul', Psa 103:1). An EXPLICIT 'you' (אַתָּה, a pronoun word) is resolved the same way — 'YOU are with me' (Psa 23:4) was left out because the rule read only the 'you' a verb carries (2026-09-26). A FEMININE 'you' or 'your' is not given a divine addressee — 'why are you downcast, O my soul' (Psa 42:12) addresses the soul — and is held (12 + 14; 2 feminine → divine remain, Psa 16:2 and 137:8). Known fault, found by the acts-of-one-agent sample: the God default misfires in calls to worship (105:1 'give thanks to the LORD'), in oracles (2:9 'you will break them'), and where a new vocative takes over (103:22) — P-2026-09-26-21. (3) WITHDRAWN 2026-09-25: 'so' in a fulfilment was a pronoun pointing at the command. Doug: כֵּן 'belongs a level higher' — it is lifted out of the clause onto the `fulfils` or `likewise` link it stood for, and is no longer a word in the content. (4) And its implicit 'they' is the ones that command chain was addressed to, walked up through `content` — 'they did so' (Exo 8:13) → Moses and Aaron, a minted composite. Rules 3 and 4 resolve by STRUCTURE, not by candidates, so they apply to plurals. (5) A clause that fulfils one command of a collection has, as its implicit subject, that command's actor: 'he struck' (Exo 8:13) fulfils 'strike', whose actor is Aaron — held by rule 1 (Aaron, Moses and the LORD all agree), resolved by the fulfilment. (7) THE HEART STANDS FOR ITS OWNER: after a clause whose subject is a heart with a named or resolved owner ('Pharaoh's heart was hardened'), an implicit subject agreeing with that owner is the owner ('and he would not listen', Exo 8:15; Doug: 'is there a way for he to resolve to Pharaoh?'). 10 resolved, 9 right — the miss is Psa 22:15, where the heart itself is the subject ('my heart ... it melted'). (6) The implicit subject of a command's EFFECT that agrees with the command's object is that object: 'strike the dust ... and it will become gnats' (Exo 8:12) → the dust; 4 in the corpus, 4 right. (8) THE PSALM'S 'ME' IS THE PSALMIST: a first-person singular pronoun — object suffix 'he makes ME lie down', 'you are with ME', the 'my' suffix node, independent אֲנִי — in a clause outside any quotation and the heading refers to the psalmist, the psalm's voice, as its 'I' (subject) and 'my' (possessor) already did; the psalmist resolves to the writer at the Writing (Doug, 2026-09-26: 'resolve me to the psalmist'). He weighed the pray-er as a second referent and set it above the structure graph, since the text does not state it. LABELS: Hebrew has no 'it', so an unresolved third-person singular is drawn 'he/it' or 'she/it' (Doug, 2026-09-25: 'the subject of he looks wrong'); resolved to a named person or God it is 'he', to a thing 'it'.

established.quote: if there is only one possible candidate for pronoun resolution in the leading text - you can resolve - if there is potential ambiguity - you hold off

relations.also: Doug, the same day: 'a general rule of thumb can be held that second person in psalms refers to God in Psalms unless overridden. Psalms 103 first few verses is an example of overriding as the Psalmist is addressing his soul' — and 'Bless the Lord, O my soul is an imperative directed at the psalmist's soul'.
relations.was: A nearest-agreeing walk (CHAIN_RESOLVE, now off): perfect on Psalm 23:2-3, 6 of 17 right corpus-wide, because narrative walks past the real antecedent (Gen 38:22 'he said' → Judah for Hirah). The unique-candidate rule does not guess.
relations.proof: Hebrew only (Greek is step 3). Rule 1: 862 singular resolved (the 2,921 before plurals were held), 10,975 held as ambiguous, 474 with no candidate, 6,112 plurals held. Samples of 16, in order of the fixes: 5 of 9 Hebrew right (a name with no recorded number agreed with 'they': 'they obey me' → the LORD); then 8 of 16 (אֱלֹהִים is plural in form, and 5 of the 8 misses were 'they' → God); with names and divine names singular, 12 of 16. Psalm 23:2-3 and 103:1-2 all right. Rule 2: 979. Rule 3: withdrawn (was 21). Rule 4: 4 (the doers of a fulfilled command). Rule 8: 1,440; a sample of 16, 15 right and 1 lexicalised (the suffix of אֲדֹנָי, 'my Lord' in form, 'the Lord' in use — MACULA Psa 77:8), which the 'my' possessor rule already treats the same way.
relations.known_fault: Animacy: a candidate that cannot act is still a candidate — 'may they rejoice' → words (Psa 35:24), 'they fly' → praise (Isa 60:8), 'they flee' → baggage (Jer 46:21). Measured for plurals 2026-09-25 after the frog plague put 'that they may sacrifice' on the rivers (Exo 8:4) and 'they piled them in heaps' on the houses (8:10): a corpus sample of plural resolutions was 8 of 16 right, against 12 of 16 singular, and plurals were 2,059 of the 2,921 written — so plurals are HELD. Separating persons from things is the meaning graph's (plan 4.3).
relations.addressee_defaults: Who 'you' is depends on the kind of text, and a vocative overrides everywhere. Built: in a psalm's own voice, God (Doug's rule of thumb), or the vocative ('O my soul', Psa 103:1). Held readings for beyond the Psalms: Micah 6:8 addresses mortals — 'O MAN' (אָדָם), a vocative (doug-047); Isaiah 55:8-9 addresses the reader, and is 'a declaration from the Lord' (doug-048) — נְאֻם יְהוָה, 'declares the LORD', a speech formula that names its sender as 'thus says the LORD' does.

relations.label: one of
relations.reads: {src} is one of, or some of, {dst}
relations.definition: Someone the text describes without naming is one of, or some of, a group it names nearby: 'a priest' of 'the priests' (Leviticus 21:1), 'the second angel' of the seven (Revelation 16:1), 'others of the Jews' (John 10:19). Always a reading (the generic check, plan 1.41), never by rule. The same term as the prepositional relation `partitive` ('one of the mountains'), so that one query finds 'one of' inside a phrase and between a person and a group.

established.note: Doug, choosing among four options for the generic check's 65 'part of' answers: 'go with partitive'. Shared with the prepositional type, as purpose and means are.

relations.label: causes
relations.deferred: Built by the earlier builder (tools/placeholders.py); the clean builder (plan 1.26) does not build it yet. Its rule, measurements and tests are kept as code for re-entry (plan 1.27).
relations.definition: A causative verb (Hebrew hiphil) holds two events: the causing, and the event caused. The outer content keeps the causer and the verb; the INNER content has the object of the causing as its subject, with the places and manner — 'he makes [me lie down in green pastures]'. Only where the root also occurs in the plain stem (qal), so a hiphil-only verb ('strike', 'save') is not split.

established.quote: assertion 3 needs to wrap me lying down in green pastures with "He makes me" - there is a layer missing

relations.why: The inner content is the same KIND of content as the plain event: 'bring up the frogs' (Exo 8:1, hiphil) wraps 'the frogs go up', which is the content of 8:2's report 'the frogs went up' (qal). A command and its fulfilment meet as one content.

relations.label: when / if / though
relations.definition: A FRONTED כִּי: a כִּי clause that comes before the clause it governs, which it sets — 'when', 'if' or 'though'; the Hebrew does not say which, so the link does not. It attaches forward, as a condition does. Fronted means: in MACULA's (flat) unit, no clause stands directly before the כִּי ('and' may: וְכִי opens a new sentence) and a clause follows the כִּי clause directly. MID-VERSE ONLY: a כִּי that opens a verse is usually 'FOR ...', the reason for the verse before, and the form does not separate it from a fronted 'though' — built for both, a sample of 12 was 3 right; those (≈298) stay unlinked and are counted (`fronted_ki_verse_initial_held`). Jer 38:15 'even if I give you advice, you will not listen'; Jer 14:12's second, 'and (though) they offer, I will not accept'. A כִּי AFTER its main clause stays `because` (or `that` after a verb of perceiving). Not 'setting': the superseded flat layer has an edge of that name (Deu 11:26 'I am setting before you').

relations.definition: A report that a command was carried out, where the text SAYS so with a pro-form: a narrative 'they did so' (עָשָׂה + כֵּן) or 'and it was so' (הָיָה + כֵּן), not negated, with no named subject, after a command. Points at the nearest preceding command in the book (not a cohortative), or at its collection. Its 'so' refers to that command unit, and its implicit 'they' to the ones the command chain was addressed to (walked up through `content`): Exo 8:13 'they did so' → Moses and Aaron, the collection 'stretch out your staff and strike the dust'. Plan 1.19. THEN, MEMBER BY MEMBER: the narrative clauses after the formula that repeat a command's verb fulfil THAT command and elaborate the formula ('Aaron stretched out ... struck'); one that repeats the command's EFFECT verb fulfils the effect ('the gnats were on man and beast' ← 'it will become gnats'), and is the `result` of the acts before it — the command's cause and effect, carried into the report. An action-state pair whose state is now a known fulfilment is removed: matched by lemma alone, it had joined the LORD's saying to Aaron's acts.

relations.label: so that
relations.definition: What an action is FOR. Two forms. (1) A command, then waw + jussive / cohortative / yiqtol in a DIFFERENT person. Looks forward, where 'because' looks back. A cohortative after a jussive is excluded: that is a promise. (2) Since 2026-09-25: a clause nested in another's prepositional role as לְ + infinitive construct — 'the magicians did so by their secret arts TO BRING FORTH the gnats' (Exo 8:14, BSB 8:18; Doug: why is it 'within'?). Not where the infinitive is the main verb's COMPLEMENT — after be able, do again, begin, finish, be willing, refuse, seek, know how, cease, hurry ('if you refuse to let them go', Exo 7:27) — nor after a speech or intention verb, where it is what was said ('Solomon purposed to build'); nor after הָיָה / נָתַן, which the form does not settle; nor the quotative לֵאמֹר. 2,180 built. MEASURED blind by two DeepSeek runs agreeing case for case: 10 of 16 before the speech exclusion, 10 of 13 of that sample after; the rest explain HOW rather than what for ('dealt wondrously') — meaning, not form. The same term as the prepositional relation `purpose` ('for an offering'), so one query finds the aim at both levels (Doug, 2026-10-17: 'share purpose like means').

scope._what: What this vocabulary deliberately does not attempt, stated so that a gap is a decision and not an oversight. Published with the vocabulary.
excludes: Relations inside one clause. This vocabulary links clauses, and groups of clauses; it does not relate the parts of one clause to each other ('not by all the people, but by the witnesses', Acts 10:41; a reason given as a noun; 'like a dove'). Those belong to the word level: the prepositional relations, and apposition and vocatives (plan 2.14). Doug, 2026-10-16, plan 1.35, first round.

rst._what: Our clause links and group roles against Rhetorical Structure Theory (Mann & Thompson 1988; the RST Discourse Treebank's Attribution), recorded 2026-09-25 (plan N.4) so a reader from that field can map ours to theirs, and so its catalogue shows relations we have not met. A mapping, not a conversion: ours stay the source. RST's NUCLEUS is our group's HEAD; its SATELLITE the qualifying member. `fit`: exact (same relation, same direction), close (see note), none (ours has no RST counterpart, or sits below or beside the discourse level). The check fails on a built clause-link or group-member relation with no entry here, and on an entry naming an undeclared relation.

purpose.note: Satellite = the purpose clause; nucleus = the command it serves.

if.note: Ours runs from the conditioned to the condition, as RST's nucleus → satellite.

condition.note: Member role inside a Conditional group.

consequence.note: Member role inside a Conditional group.

until_limit.note: A temporal limit; RST's Circumstance sets a frame, where 'until' bounds the clause.

describing.note: A participle describing the subject as it acts (Circumstance) or who it is (Elaboration).

contrast.note: RST's Contrast is multinuclear; here the second clause is linked from the first. Some are Concession — a reading.

but_rather.note: Not X but Y: the rejected and the affirmed. The 'except' sense is closer to RST's Otherwise/Exception, which RST does not name.

when_if_though.note: A fronted כִּי: RST would choose one of the three by reading; the Hebrew states only that the clause sets the one after it.

attached.note: A satellite of a command whose relation the form does not decide; RST would name it by reading. Ours records only that a connective attaches it (plan 1.42, 2026-10-18).

undecided.note: Not a relation but its candidates: the form does not decide, so the link lists them (a verse-opening כִּי, 'for' or 'when'). RST would pick one by reading; ours declines to (plan 1.42, 2026-10-17, on its being marked built).

sequence.note: Multinuclear. Ours is marked by the fused waw of wayyiqtol / weqatal.

lest.note: RST's Otherwise: realizing the nucleus prevents the satellite. 'Do this lest that' fits; a bare 'lest' after an assertion is rarer.

because.note: RST splits a stated reason three ways by the WRITER'S INTENT — the reason for the event, for saying it, or for believing it. That is a reading; the text marks one relation (כִּי, יַעַן, עֵקֶב), so we keep one.

basis.note: RST's Motivation: the satellite raises the hearer's desire to do the nucleus — 'give thanks to the LORD, FOR he is good' (Psa 107:1). Ours is a member role of an Imperative group.

aim.note: Member role of an Imperative group.

command.note: The head of an Imperative group.

warning.note: RST's Otherwise: if the nucleus (the command) is not realized, the satellite (the warning) will be. 'Do not go up, lest you be struck down' (Num 14:42). Member role of an Imperative group (2026-10-18).

therefore.note: RST splits Volitional / Non-volitional Result by intent; as with because, we keep one.

failed_result.note: RST's Result, with the outcome that the purpose was not achieved; RST has no failure relation.

as.note: Comparison is not in RST's classic set; the nearest, Elaboration or Evidence, would drop the 'just as'. Where the compared clause is a saying it asserts fulfilment of a word, which RST also lacks.

likewise.note: One agent repeating another's deed, across verses; RST's Joint or Sequence would drop the sameness the text asserts with כֵּן.

elaborates.note: The satellite gives detail of the nucleus. First met 2026-09-25, Exo 8:13: 'Aaron stretched out ... and struck' is the detail of 'this they did'.

fulfils.note: Fulfilment of a command — across verses, by a pro-form ('they did so'). RST relates adjacent spans and has no fulfilment relation; nearest is Volitional Result, which would assert a cause the text does not state.

result.note: The commanded act as the nucleus, what it brings about as the satellite. RST's Result, not split by intent.

effect.note: Member role of an Imperative group; see result.

and.note: Multinuclear. RST's List asks that the members be comparable, which is a reading; ours is the separate-word waw.

its_ground.note: Why the nucleus holds despite the satellite — RST has no single relation for a concession's reason.

described_as.note: Members of a Descriptions group: a list, each elaborating the common referent.

agent_act.note: An AgentActs group's members: a multinuclear list of one agent's acts. RST's Joint does not say the agent is shared; the group's subject does.

line.note: A Parallel group's lines. Synonymous parallelism reads as Restatement — a reading; the structure marks only the parallel.

content.note: RST-DT's Attribution: the reporting clause and what is reported. Ours embeds the said clause in the saying.

that.note: Know / see / hear THAT — complement clauses, which classic RST leaves below the discourse level and RST-DT treats as Attribution.

within.note: Syntactic nesting of a clause in another's role: below the level RST relates.

causes.note: Causation inside ONE verb (the hiphil): two events in a single word, below the level of spans.

action.note: The command-then-report pair ('let there be light / there was light'): fulfilment, which RST does not name. Nearest is Volitional Result, which would assert a cause the text does not state (the reading withdrawn at Genesis 1:3).

frame.note: Communication layer: the clause a communication is said in.

part.note: Communication layer: what a communication contains.

not_yet_met._what: RST relations with no counterpart in our graph yet — each a question to put to the next passages, not a kind to add.
not_yet_met.Circumstance: 'When ...' — the frame an event happens in. Candidate marker: a preposition governing an infinitive clause (בְּ / כְּ + infinitive), which is exactly the 579 PP2CL wrappers of plan 1.15.
not_yet_met.Contrast / Antithesis: 'But', 'but rather' — כִּי אִם, אֲבָל, אַךְ, ἀλλά. Unbuilt, and common.
not_yet_met.Background: What a reader needs to understand the nucleus. Unmarked; meaning.
not_yet_met.Means: 'By doing X'. Candidate marker: בְּ + infinitive again, read differently.
not_yet_met.Evaluation / Interpretation: The writer's assessment of what was said. Unmarked; meaning.
not_yet_met.Summary / Restatement: Restatement shares a shape with parallelism (see line).
not_yet_met.Solutionhood: A problem and its answer. Unmarked.
not_yet_met.Enablement: Satellite makes the nucleus possible. Unmarked.
not_yet_met.Preparation: Text that readies the reader — a heading. Our psalm heading, the Writing's frame, may be it.

forces._what: The force of a clause, in two layers. `asserts.force` holds the LANGUAGE'S FORM (wayyiqtol, subjunctive ...); `asserts.upper` and the clause's `upper_force` hold the MEANING-LAYER force it maps to below — built 2026-09-25, so a Greek and a Hebrew clause can meet at 'assertion'. The form stays on the Verb node too. The mapping is by form, and a form is not always its force: the cautions say where.

families._what: The five families of speech act (Searle), adopted 2026-09-25 as the FRAME for force (plan N.3) — because it was free and shows what is missing. A family is admitted only where the text MARKS it: a verb form, a formula, a performative verb, an interjection. Form is not act: a family is recorded beside the form-derived force, never instead of it, and the cautions say where they part. Doug: 'conform if it is free or helpful - but do not conform if we give up something meaningfully important'.

list.definition: Commits the speaker to something being so.
list.via: the upper force 'assertion', from the verb form (and verbless clauses).

list.definition: Tries to get the hearer to do something.
list.via: the upper force 'directive', from imperative, jussive, cohortative, Greek imperative and hortatory subjunctive.

list.definition: Commits the SPEAKER to a future act: a promise, an oath, a vow.
list.markers: Measured 2026-09-25 in MACULA: שָׁבַע 'swear' niphal 154, hiphil 31; נָדַר 'vow' 31; ὀμνύω 26. And 'do this and live' — a command with a promise (plan 1.6).
list.why_not_built: Markers exist; which clause each governs (the oath's content) is unbuilt.

list.definition: Expresses the speaker's attitude: praise, thanks, blessing, woe, lament.
list.markers: Measured 2026-09-25: woe — הוֹי 51, אוֹי 24, οὐαί 46; blessed — בָּרוּךְ (passive participle) 77, μακάριος 50, εὐλογητός 8, and אַשְׁרֵי; thank — εὐχαριστέω 38.
list.caution: 'Praise the LORD' (הַלְלוּ, piel imperative, 52) and 'give thanks' (הוֹדוּ, 18) are imperatives: DIRECTIVE by form, expressive as acts. Psalm 103:1 'bless the LORD, O my soul' is both at once. A family is recorded beside the form's force, never replacing it.
list.why_not_built: Markers exist; the psalms' expressive character (Doug: illustration 'makes up most of the psalms') is largely unmarked and needs meaning.

list.definition: An utterance that makes what it says so by saying it: naming, appointing, pronouncing ('you are my son; today I have begotten you', Psa 2:7, is a candidate).
list.caution: NOT the formula נְאֻם יְהוָה, 'utterance of the LORD' (376): that names WHO speaks, which is the communication layer's sender, not a force. Doug called Isaiah 55:8-9 'a declaration from the Lord' (doug-048); in this vocabulary it is an assertive whose sender the formula marks. Found by reading the definition, not the name — the kind of mismatch 'conform where free' has to watch for.

upper.label: directive
upper.definition: Tells someone to do or be something: command, let, let us.

upper.label: assertion
upper.definition: States that something is, was or will be so — including a VERBLESS clause: 'the LORD is my shepherd', 'your word is a lamp'.

upper.label: wish
upper.definition: Wants something to be so without commanding it.
upper.family_note: No single family: a wish may be expressive (the Greek optative, 'may it be') or near-directive (a jussive to a third party). Kept as its own until what marks the difference is measured.

upper.label: not finite
upper.definition: An infinitive heading a clause, or a Greek participle: says an act without asserting it.
upper.family_note: Not an act, so in no family.

upper.label: no verb
upper.definition: Verbless clauses as having no force.
upper.instead: assertion (2026-09-25): 'the LORD is my shepherd' is verbless and plainly asserts; a force of 'none' would have kept Doug's illustration from being an assertion at all.

yiqtol.caution: Also a prohibition after לֹא and a wish in poetry. The form is not always the force.

participle active.gloss: is doing / is about to do
participle active.caution: Heading a clause, a participle IS the predicate: 'I am about to strike your territory' (Exo 7:27) states something imminent. First mapped 'not finite', which the frog-plague drawing showed wrong on 2026-09-24. Attributive participles do not head clauses, so they never reach this table.

participle passive.caution: As the active participle: heading a clause, it is the predicate.

-.caution: Most verbless clauses assert (identity, attribute, location); some are questions or exclamations, which no form marks.

subjunctive.caution: Hortatory in a main clause, purpose or condition in a subordinate one. The form is not the force.
